audit.why: On disk the chart reads Dr. Mundo, Skill, Singed, Singed, Dr. Mundo, Singed, Singed — four Singed stages on a lane he wins 52.55% over 1237 games, with Mundo owning level 1 and the Maximum Dosage spike at 6. That matches the prose at every row. The singed packet's defect line describes a different, Mundo-favoured chart; that snapshot does not match what is actually in champ-data.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere, and level 3 is credited to a Heart Zapper 'stun' that does not exist.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17s at rank 1 and Riot's text gives it persistent damage, damage storage and a burst that heals — no stun of any kind. Infected Bonesaw is 4s and scales on current health, not max. Maximum Dosage is 120s. Blunt Force Trauma is 9s and is the auto-reset.
audit.corrected: 17s, 4s, 120s and 9s written in; the invented stun removed from whys[2] and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this lane is absent from both layers: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him, which means your Fling — a displacement — is simply eaten, and he drops a cannister that heals him when he walks over it. Everything the entry tells you to do with Fling assumes it lands. Also wants.foe[1] calls Heart Zapper his E (it is W; E is Blunt Force Trauma), and wants.you[2] says Rylai's 'permanently roots him' when it slows.
audit.why: Riot text — Dr. Mundo P: 'Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby. Dr. Mundo can pick it up by walking over it, restoring Health.' Singed E flings and knocks up, which is exactly the class of effect that passive is built to eat. Singed R: 'making his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds' — the direct answer to both Heart Zapper's heal and Maximum Dosage's missing-health heal.
audit.corrected: The passive is stated with the play that follows from it — bait it with a throwaway Fling, then glue and flip for real — plus correct slots, the real slow, and the anti-heal timing rule 'ult before he ults'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing about the cannister his passive drops.
audit.why: Walking over it restores health and reduces the passive's cooldown, so the immobilise-resist comes back faster if he collects it — which changes how soon your real Fling can land.

edits.before: Level 1 and 2 are an honest mirror of weaknesses — neither of you can actually kill the other, but Mundo's Infected Bonesaw (Q) cleaver can percent-HP poke you off the wave if you walk in a straight line. Don't stand still and absorb Qs; keep moving erratically and get Poison Trail ticks on the wave rather than trying to run him over. Level 3 is where he pulls ahead briefly: Heart Zapper gives him a damage-and-stun tool that punishes your Fling approach, and his passive health-bar ticking means your poison ramps slower than his self-heal. Accept that you are not winning a trade here and start your proxy pattern — get between his tower and his wave, force him to make a choice, and never stand in Bonesaw range waiting for a fight that does not favour you yet.
edits.after: Levels 1 and 2 are an honest mirror of weaknesses — neither of you can kill the other, but Infected Bonesaw (4s) chips a share of your current health if you walk in a straight line. Keep moving erratically and put Poison Trail through the wave instead. Learn the one rule that decides this lane now: Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him, so your first Fling is simply eaten, and the cannister he drops heals him and shortens that passive if he walks over it. Spend a throwaway Fling to burn it, deny the pickup, and keep the real flip for after. Level 3 is briefly his — Heart Zapper stores your poison and gives it back as a heal — so start proxying rather than waiting for a trade that does not favour you yet.

notes: The lane-deciding interaction was missing from both layers: Dr. Mundo's passive eats the first immobilizing effect, which is precisely Singed's Fling, and the cannister it drops heals him and refreshes the resist sooner if he collects it. Every Fling instruction in this entry assumed the flip lands. Also removed a Heart Zapper 'stun' that does not exist in Riot's text, corrected Heart Zapper from E to W, and corrected 'permanently roots' to slows.
